transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-11-08
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Chen (Redwood SE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood CSM), Sarah Nguyen (Evercrest Head ML), Omar Haddad (Evercrest Infra), Priya Rao (Evercrest Security), Benji Park (Evercrest Product)

Summary: exploratory migration readiness call — Evercrest is evaluating moving parts of their LLM stack off their managed Anthrapic/OpenAI stack and into either Redwood Hosted, Redwood Dedicated, or a Private VPC deployment. Primary concerns: eval parity (quality and hallucination profile), latency at 100k daily active users, quantization/FP16 behavior, KV cache compatibility, and enterprise controls (KMS, SSO, audit logs, data residency).

00:00 Maya Patel: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we, from Redwood, appreciate the time. quick roundtable — say who you are.
00:07 Sarah Nguyen: hi, Sarah here, Head of ML at Evercrest. we run the recommender + assistant stack. currently on Anthrapic and some Azure OpenAI for experiments.
00:11 Omar Haddad: Omar, infra. we manage the cluster, networking, cost controls.
00:14 Priya Rao: Priya, security and compliance. SOC2 in progress, lots of questions about KMS and audit trails.
00:18 Benji Park: Benji, product, focusing on latency targets for web UX.
00:22 Diego Chen: diego from Redwood, SE — i'll lead the technical deep dive and perf questions.
00:26 Maya Patel: and I'll own commercial + next steps. cool. agenda, quick: current stack + pain points, target metrics, hosting options and tradeoffs, sample pilot and benchmarks, security checklist, next steps. ok?

02:01 Sarah: yeah, let me give some context — we ship a multi-turn assistant embedded in our dashboard and an in-product code helper. production is c.100k DAU, tokens vary a lot, 30–600 token responses. we've been on Anthrapic ClaudeX for most things and OpenAI for a few features. lately costs have spiked and latency variability is hurting conversions. we also want more control over model pinning and rollouts.

03:05 Diego: understandable. when you say latency variability, are we seeing tail latency spikes from cold KV cache misses or from the provider side? any quant numbers?
03:12 Sarah: yeah, 95p around 600–1,200 ms on hosted right now, sometimes 2s during peak. we want steady < 400ms 95p ideally.

04:30 Omar: also we have regulatory constraints in EU region — some customers need data residency plus separate key management. we want option to run in our VPC or an on-prem box for a subset of workloads.

05:12 Priya: and for us encryption in transit and at rest is table stakes; we also want HSM-backed KMS, RBAC, SSO/SAML and immutable audit logs.

06:00 Diego: ok, so three hosting modes fit — hosted for fastest time-to-value, dedicated for predictable throughput and isolation, and private VPC/on-prem for full control. tradeoffs: hosted is easiest but less isolation; dedicated gives reserved capacity and SLA; private adds ops overhead but meets strict compliance. for parity with Anthrapic/OpenAI models, our model catalog and deployment options support variant pinning and rollbacks.

07:05 Benji: question: we use a custom fine-tuned variant on ClaudeX — how easy is it to port weights or replicate behavior?
07:18 Diego: short answer: depends. if you have checkpoints compatible with the open formats we support, we can onboard and run evals. in many cases, parity is about prompt engineering + temperature and sampling configs. sometimes quantization changes tokens slightly — we'll run eval parity.

09:30 Sarah: you mentioned v-lm and TGI earlier, we run vLLM in prod behind a kong gateway for a microservice. we also spin up T-G-I on GKE for some heavy batch jobs. how compatible is Redwood with those runtimes?
09:51 Diego: we often see customers migrating off v-lm/TGI. Redwood supports the same model families; our runtime has optimized kernels and KV cache flow. caveat: v-lm request batching semantics differ, so we typically run a small compatibility test to match KV cache keys and streaming hooks. sometimes minor prompt rewrite needed.

11:40 Omar: about cost — we need to compare unit token cost, dedicated reserved capacity shipping cost, and burst options. do you have a spreadsheet?
11:50 Maya: yes, we'll share a benchmark + pricing spreadsheet. it'll include hosted per-token, Dedicated reserved hourly with burst, and ballpark private deployment TCO.

13:02 Priya: on security docs — we need SOC2, ISO27001, penetration test reports and KMS integration guide. do you have those?
13:12 Liam Ortiz: liam here, i'll drop the security pack to your SSO-protected share. includes SOC2 summary, ISO artifacts, and KMS/HSM integration notes.

14:30 Sarah: for eval parity — we have a 120-sample prompt set plus production logs for hallucination analysis. can you run quality regression checks automatically?
14:42 Diego: yes. Redwood Optimize and our eval harness can run prompt sets against target model variants and produce diff reports for token-level differences, Rouge-style metrics and hallucination counts. we can also run A/B canary rollouts.

16:00 Benji: what's the ramp plan? pilot on hosted and then switch to dedicated?
16:08 Maya: common path — start hosted to validate parity quickly, then if throughput/latency/cost needs demand, move to Dedicated or Private. we can also run a hybrid: sensitive traffic to Private, lower-risk to Hosted.

18:05 Omar: network egress and VPC peering — if we do Private, how do we handle peering? do you do direct connect to cloud regions?
18:15 Diego: for Private we have a VPC connector pattern and can do cross-account peering or VPN. for on-prem there's an agent model; could be heavier ops. we'll diagram options in the follow-up doc.

20:30 Priya: auditing — do you preserve per-request audit logs and token-level traces? retention controls?
20:42 Liam Ortiz: yes — we have token-level traces and request logs with configurable retention; enterprise packages include long-term retention and exports to your SIEM.

22:05 Sarah: some parts of our stack need sub-200ms p95 for short queries (30–80 tokens). can Redwood hit that on Dedicated?
22:15 Diego: many customers hit <200ms p95 on dedicated with optimized kernels and prefix caching. depends on model size, quantization profile, and sequence length. if you share sample traffic we'll run a benchmark.

24:00 Omar: we run an 8k context usage for some call-history features. how does Redwood handle long context and kv cache?
24:10 Diego: runtime supports large context windows with efficient KV cache sharding. cost grows but we do prefix caching and hot-key caching to keep latency low. we should test with your 8k sequences specifically.

26:30 Sarah: any gotchas with quantization? we use 4-bit QAT in prod sometimes, and TGI had some mismatches.
26:40 Diego: quantization can impact output subtleties; we have quantization profiles and suggestions per workload. we'll recommend a profile and run evals to check for regression. sometimes a hybrid FP16 for few layers helps.

29:00 Benji: timeline — we want a decision before end of quarter. is two-week pilot realistic?
29:09 Maya: yes, 2–3 week pilot doable: one week onboarding + data prep, one week perf + quality parity, final week review.

31:20 Priya: legal/procurement — contracts need data processing addendum and standard indemnities. we have an internal buyer who will loop in legal.
31:30 Maya: noted — we have standard DPA templates, and enterprise contracts for Dedicated/Private.

33:00 Omar: how do you handle model updates/rollouts? we need pinning and canary.
33:07 Diego: model versioning is first-class; rollouts support canary %, automatic fallback to previous variant on error, and traffic splitting.

35:40 Sarah: a weird but real ask — we use a mix of ClaudeX fine-tunes plus some OpenAI function calling at times. function calling parity — how robust is that?
35:55 Diego: we support function/tool calling semantics; there may be small mapping differences in annotation but we can replicate with adapter layers. we'll test your function patterns in the parity run.

38:10 Benji: any notable customers in our space who've migrated? examples help sell internally.
38:17 Maya: yes — a fintech player moved to Dedicated for latency and cost and reported 35% lower TCO and improved p95. we can share anonymized case study.

40:00 Speaker 3 (interrupt / muffled): uh quick — can you, uh, also show what fallback looks like when region overwhelmed?
40:08 Diego: yes, automatic routing policies can route to alternate region or model variant; for strict data residency we keep local only. fallback policies are configurable.

42:12 Priya: on keys, do you offer KMS integration with customer's cloud KMS and HSM?
42:20 Liam Ortiz: yes, support for AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and external HSM via key wrap. we'll include the integration guide.

44:00 Sarah: ok agreed — let's do pilot on hosted first targeting the assistant flow. Diego to run parity tests vs our v-lm/TGI config.
44:08 Diego: yep I'll need the prompt corpus and your v-lm/TGI config and any quantization flags.
44:20 Sarah: i'll upload those to the share — anonymized logs and prompt set.

46:30 Maya: to recap, action items — Redwood send benchmark + pricing + security pack; Evercrest provides prompt set + 3 days traffic; Diego runs perf parity; meet back in ~2 weeks.

47:10 Priya: small note — please redact PII from logs; we will only share anonymized traces.
47:15 Maya: yes we'll only ask for anonymized.

49:00 Benji: last thing — SLA targets and escalation path for Dedicated?
49:07 Maya: Dedicated comes with SLA and a named technical contact, we can include escalation matrix in proposal.

51:20 Sarah: timeline check — if we start onboarding next week, results by two weeks out?
51:28 Diego: yes, likely. exact timing depends on your data handoff.

53:00 Speaker 3: thanks everyone, this was helpful

53:10 Maya: thanks all. i'll email the spreadsheet and a calendar for the follow-up.

54:00 Session end — some crosstalk and off-mic chatter.

Notes on transcription quality: medium — a couple of names were garbled (Anthrapic), "v-lm" written in notes as vLLM sometimes, timestamps roughly every 30–90s. Shared artifacts referenced: https://redwood.link/benchmarks (benchmark spreadsheet), https://redwood.link/security-pack (security pack), and a placeholder for the customer's secure upload link.

End of transcript.
